attributes.description:
Estimated coefficients for the linear predictor (`X @ coef_ +
intercept_`) in the GLM.
attributes.name: coef_

attributes.description: Intercept (a.k.a. bias) added to linear predictor.
attributes.name: intercept_

attributes.description:
Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.

.. versionadded:: 0.24
attributes.name: n_features_in_

attributes.description:
Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
has feature names that are all strings.

.. versionadded:: 1.0
attributes.name: feature_names_in_

attributes.description: Actual number of iterations used in the solver.
attributes.name: n_iter_

methods.name: get_metadata_routing
methods.summary: Get metadata routing of this object.

methods.name: predict
methods.summary: Predict using GLM with feature matrix X.

methods.name: score
methods.summary: Compute D^2, the percentage of deviance explained.

methods.name: set_fit_request
methods.summary: Configure whether metadata should be requested to be passed to the ``fit`` method.

methods.name: set_params
methods.summary: Set the parameters of this estimator.

methods.name: set_score_request
methods.summary: Configure whether metadata should be requested to be passed to the ``score`` method.

parameters.description:
Constant that multiplies the L2 penalty term and determines the
regularization strength. ``alpha = 0`` is equivalent to unpenalized
GLMs. In this case, the design matrix `X` must have full column rank
(no collinearities).
Values of `alpha` must be in the range `[0.0, inf)`.
parameters.name: alpha

parameters.description:
Specifies if a constant (a.k.a. bias or intercept) should be
added to the linear predictor (`X @ coef + intercept`).
parameters.name: fit_intercept

parameters.description:
Algorithm to use in the optimization problem:

'lbfgs'
    Calls scipy's L-BFGS-B optimizer.

'newton-cholesky'
    Uses Newton-Raphson steps (in arbitrary precision arithmetic equivalent to
    iterated reweighted least squares) with an inner Cholesky based solver.
    This solver is a good choice for `n_samples` >> `n_features`, especially
    with one-hot encoded categorical features with rare categories. Be aware
    that the memory usage of this solver has a quadratic dependency on
    `n_features` because it explicitly computes the Hessian matrix.

    .. versionadded:: 1.2
parameters.name: solver

parameters.description:
The maximal number of iterations for the solver.
Values must be in the range `[1, inf)`.
parameters.name: max_iter

parameters.description:
Stopping criterion. For the lbfgs solver,
the iteration will stop when ``max{|g_j|, j = 1, ..., d} <= tol``
where ``g_j`` is the j-th component of the gradient (derivative) of
the objective function.
Values must be in the range `(0.0, inf)`.
parameters.name: tol

parameters.description:
If set to ``True``, reuse the solution of the previous call to ``fit``
as initialization for ``coef_`` and ``intercept_`` .
parameters.name: warm_start

parameters.description:
For the lbfgs solver set verbose to any positive number for verbosity.
Values must be in the range `[0, inf)`.
parameters.name: verbose

signature: PoissonRegressor(*, alpha=1.0, fit_intercept=True, solver='lbfgs', max_iter=100, tol=0.0001, warm_start=False, verbose=0)
summary: Generalized Linear Model with a Poisson distribution.
